text:
maya: starting a small canary publish for py + ts SDKs in ~10m. will use `redwood-canary` dist-tag and testpypi. giving heads-up for infra pinning. :eyes:

sam: ack. what's the rollout criteria? failures threshold / time window?

maya: plan: 50 canary users for 30m. rollback if error rate > 3% OR tokenization mismatch on embeddings. auto-rollback enabled in deploy bot.

liam: noted. i'll pin internal platform-api client deps to 2.3.1 in the canary branch so we don't get accidental drift.

maya: thanks. publish commands i'll run:
```
# npm
npm publish ./packages/js --tag redwood-canary
# python
python -m build && twine upload -r testpypi dist/*
```

eva: quick ask — we need the deprecation warning baked into the Python package for legacy sync (v0.x) so users get one release notice. add a CHANGES entry and a runtime warn.

maya: will add runtime warning: `warnings.warn("legacy sync client deprecated, see migration guide", DeprecationWarning)` and CHANGES.md entry. deprecation timeline: soft deprecate now (warn for 2 releases), hard remove in 2.0.0 in ~8 weeks.

sam: fgts (fine-grained traffic steering) for canary? route only to hosted tier and Dedicated non-prod pools, not to production Dedicated.

maya: yes, only hosted sandbox + dedicated-staging. will avoid prod tiers.

deploy-bot: publish started: js@1.5.0-canary.2025.04. flag: redwood-canary. CI jobs triggered.

ci-bot: smoke-tests started for js & py packages. e2e matrix: node14/18, py38/310.

liam: I see a flaky test in the react example on node14 last night. if it flakes in canary, let's not rollback automatically — instead triage for 30m then decide. can we set rollback policy to manual for that specific failure class?

maya: ok changed policy: automatic rollback for server errors (5xx) and generation mismatches; manual for client-side example flakiness.

ci-bot: smoke-tests: js node18 passed, node14 failed (react example timeout).

sam: timeout logs? share snippet.

ci-bot: ```
react-example.test.js › should render with streaming
  Error: Timeout of 120000ms exceeded.
  at Timeout._onTimeout (jest.js:456)
```

liam: that's the flaky one. per policy we won't auto-rollback. sam / maya — you ok to continue?

sam: yes continue. keep monitoring and check analytics for an uptick in error budget. if we hit 5% errors for generated responses then rollback.

maya: canary metrics dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/canary/1742009999 (will populate in 2m). alert thresholds set.

deploy-bot: publish finished for js. py wheels uploaded to testpypi. artifacts: js@1.5.0-canary.2025.04, py@0.11.0rc1-canary. logs: https://ci.redwood/builds/5643

eva: reminder: update docs site with deprecation note and link to migration guide once release is stable. I'll draft the short blurb.

maya: monitoring: if embedding similarity distribution shifts > 0.02 L2 or response latency increases > 30% for canary cohort, we auto-rollback.

ci-bot: canary metrics heartbeat OK. 2m in: errors 0.8%, latency +8%.

maya: good. leaving canary running. tagging internal release notes draft now.

sam: one more ops ask — when we switch dist-tag from `redwood-canary` to `latest` for the final publish, please call out in #eng-releases 1h in advance.

maya: will do. planning final cut tomorrow in change window 03:00 UTC.

liam: and we'll push an npm dist-tag deprecate note to customers using legacy tags. I'll coordinate with sales for any flagged customers.

maya: thanks all. ping me if alerts fire. :shipit:

deploy-bot: NOTE: if rollback triggered, artifacts will be untagged and a revert PR will be created: redwood/sdk-releases#321

sam: tldr; canary in progress, auto-rollback for server/gen mismatches, manual for known client flake, deprecation warnings added to py, final cut planned tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
